smell_elimination.justification: The refactoring successfully removes all three template methods (_get_transform_context, _validate_transform_input, _compute_transform_diagnostics) from TransformerMixin and extracts them into a new ContextAwareTransformerMixin. The base TransformerMixin.fit_transform is restored to its original, clean implementation without context management calls. Only minor traces remain: the _TransformContextManager import and infrastructure in _set_output.py appears unused after this change, and Pipeline._propagate_step_contexts may need adjustment.

cross_file_coordination.justification: The refactoring correctly updates all three files: base.py (splits the mixin), _base.py in decomposition (updates _BasePCA to inherit ContextAwareTransformerMixin), and _base.py in feature_selection (updates SelectorMixin similarly). The coordination is nearly complete, though the diff doesn't show whether Pipeline._propagate_step_contexts or _TransformContextManager were adjusted to work with the new opt-in model, which could leave some orphaned infrastructure.

structural_soundness.justification: Excellent application of Interface Segregation Principle. The solution creates a proper inheritance hierarchy where TransformerMixin provides core transformation functionality, and ContextAwareTransformerMixin extends it with optional advanced features. This allows transformers to opt-in to context management only when needed. The separation of concerns is clean, responsibilities are well-defined, and the single responsibility principle is restored to TransformerMixin.

code_quality.justification: The code is clean, well-documented, and follows scikit-learn conventions. The new ContextAwareTransformerMixin includes comprehensive docstrings with examples. Method signatures and implementations are clear. The only minor issue is that the docstring example for ContextAwareTransformerMixin could be more illustrative of the context propagation benefits, but this is a very minor point.

interface_decomposition.justification: Perfect decomposition along cohesive responsibility boundaries. TransformerMixin handles core transformation (fit_transform, set_output), while ContextAwareTransformerMixin handles context propagation, validation hooks, and diagnostics. Each interface has a single, well-defined purpose. The boundary is exactly where it should be: basic transformation vs. advanced context-aware transformation.

split_quality.justification: All unnecessary stubs are removed from TransformerMixin. The granularity is appropriate - not too coarse (all in one interface) nor too fine (separate mixins for each of the three methods). The two-level hierarchy (TransformerMixin → ContextAwareTransformerMixin) strikes the right balance. Minor deduction because the diff doesn't show removal of now-unused _TransformContextManager infrastructure, suggesting possible over-engineering in the supporting code.

transformermixin_interface_segregation.justification: Exemplary fix of the core ISP violation. All three template methods are completely removed from TransformerMixin and moved to ContextAwareTransformerMixin. The base fit_transform is restored to its original, clean implementation with no context management calls. Transformers now explicitly opt-in by inheriting from ContextAwareTransformerMixin (as shown with _BasePCA and SelectorMixin). TransformerMixin returns to its focused scope of providing fit_transform and set_output. This is exactly the right solution.

aspect_3_judge.summary: This is an excellent refactoring that properly applies the Interface Segregation Principle. The solution cleanly extracts context management, validation, and diagnostics into a separate ContextAwareTransformerMixin, allowing transformers to opt-in only when needed. TransformerMixin is restored to its original focused responsibility, and all affected classes are correctly updated to use the new inheritance structure.
